chapter: Teaching, race and the future of jazz
title: Jazz is dead: Monk's illness and the black man owed a living
summary: Mingus insists the American black man's jazz is for the archives, with Dizzy and Monk gone.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, I told you before, it's dead, it's gone.
You really think the music is dead?
The American black man were the ones who created jazz. Their art is for the arcaves. Is that how you say it?
Arcaves sounds much better. Then they're really gone. Why are you so definite on that, that it's gone?
Dizzy's gone, and Monk is gone.
Yeah. What is the matter with him? Is it depression or something else?
Probably the same thing that's wrong with me. He's probably sick.
I went to the (unintelligible) all the time.
Yeah. You were saying that after the next generation --
Paul said that they gave electric shock treatments to Monk, at the hospital. He thought that might have had something to do with it. After he saw One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest, (inaudible).
I don't know. I never heard that before. He was very moved by that film.
They imported in West Indians in the black man's world. The black man wants to be on welfare and do nothing. They feel the world owes them a living, which they're right. You understand?
The world does owe the black man a
living, and they ain't taking it. I told you, this drummer that just got onto welfare?
